mechanism: MS-DECOMPOSE-SCRIPT (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1654) checks push minimality only for OP_PUSHDATA1 and OP_PUSHDATA2 (the (< len 76) test at :1686 and (< len 256) at :1697); the direct-push branch at :1678 accepts any 1..75-byte push without ever comparing it to the shortest encoding, so a one-byte push of 1..16 (which must be OP_1..OP_16) or of 0x81 (which must be OP_1NEGATE) is admitted. Core runs CheckMinimalPush(push_data, opcode) on every pushdata opcode inside DecomposeScript and returns {} when it fails (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.cpp:396-397, CheckMinimalPush at refs/bitcoin/src/script/script.cpp:373-396). Separately, %MS-OP-NUMBER (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1729) reads up to four bytes little-endian and rejects only a set sign bit; it never enforces CScriptNum's minimal encoding, so a number carrying a redundant trailing 0x00 is still a number here. Core builds CScriptNum(in.second, /*fRequireMinimal=*/true) inside a try/catch in ParseScriptNumber (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.cpp:407-419), so such a byte string is not a number and the fragment is not recognised. The two checks are independent, and we are missing both.
consequence: Two distinct scripts map onto one miniscript, which is precisely the one-to-one property inference exists to guarantee: the inferred node re-serialises to bytes different from the ones it was given, so Core's own round-trip assertion (miniscript_tests.cpp:469) does not hold here. The reachable path is signrawtransactionwithkey / signrawtransactionwithwallet, whose miniscript arm (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:469) infers a node from a CALLER-SUPPLIED witnessScript and signs it; Core refuses to sign the same input because FromScript returns nullopt. The divergence is one-directional and bounded, which is why this stays S3 rather than S2: the witness we produce is a CORRECT satisfaction of the bytes as they will execute (consensus does not set SCRIPT_VERIFY_MINIMALDATA, so [0a 00] still reads as 10 at OP_CSV), and our own wallet cannot generate such a script -- ms-node-script always emits the minimal encoding, so this requires an externally supplied witnessScript. What the operator actually gets is a fully signed transaction that mempool policy rejects as non-standard (MINIMALDATA is in STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS) and that Core would have declined to sign at all, plus an inferred descriptor/address that does not reproduce the input script.

Five divergences, each accepted here and rejected by Core: '010ab2' (one-byte push of 10, then OP_CSV) -> 'older(10)', reser '5ab2', roundtrip NIL; '010ab1' -> 'after(10)', reser '5ab1', roundtrip NIL; '020a00b2' (push of [0a 00], a non-minimal CScriptNum) -> 'older(10)', reser '5ab2', roundtrip NIL; '020a00b1' -> 'after(10)', roundtrip NIL; and the non-minimal multi counts '0101<21 K1><21 K2>0102ae' -> multi(1,K1,K2) re-serialising to the OP_1/OP_2 form, roundtrip NIL. Negative controls confirm the check is not simply absent everywhere: '028000b2' is a MINIMAL two-byte CScriptNum (128) and is accepted by both, roundtrip T; '0181b2' (one-byte push of 0x81) -> NIL here as well, because %ms-op-number rejects the sign bit; '4c0120b1' (PUSHDATA1 of one byte) -> NIL; and Core's own two negative unit vectors, the nonminpush script (miniscript_tests.cpp:650) and the non-minimal VERIFY script (miniscript_tests.cpp:654), both -> NIL here. Core side read at d3056bc: miniscript.cpp:396-397 and :407-419, script.cpp:373-396. Ours: src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1654, :1678, :1686, :1697, :1729; call site src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:469.
fix_shape: Port CheckMinimalPush verbatim as a helper and call it from the two places Core calls it. In MS-DECOMPOSE-SCRIPT, apply it to every pushdata branch, not just the PUSHDATA1/2 ones: for a direct push of 1..75 bytes reject when the payload is a single byte in 1..16 (OP_1..OP_16 were required) or the single byte 0x81 (OP_1NEGATE was required); the existing length tests already cover the PUSHDATA1/PUSHDATA2 cases and the opcode == data.size() case is structural for a direct push. Keep the OP_0 / OP_1..OP_16 normalisations Core makes BEFORE the check, since CheckMinimalPush is asserted never to see those opcodes (script.cpp:374-375). In %MS-OP-NUMBER, add CScriptNum's minimal-encoding rule -- for a non-empty payload, if the last byte masked with 0x7f is zero then the encoding is minimal only when the payload is longer than one byte and the second-to-last byte has 0x80 set -- and return NIL otherwise, so the fragment simply is not recognised rather than signalling. Guard both with the positive controls above, in particular '028000b2' (minimal 128, must stay accepted) next to '020a00b2' (must become NIL), so the new check cannot pass by rejecting everything. Then re-run Core's 91 vectors in both contexts to confirm no legitimate script regressed.
